common_name: Pugster Blue Butterfly Bush (Dwarf Sterile Reblooming Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Pugster Blue is a compact, sterile, non-invasive butterfly bush that stays under 2 feet tall, fitting into small garden beds and large containers where standard butterfly bush is too large.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Pugster Blue is part of the Pugster series of dwarf butterfly bushes, bred to stay compact — under 2 feet tall and wide — while producing full-sized, densely packed, true-blue flower spikes on unusually thick, sturdy stems that hold up well without flopping. Unlike older Buddleja davidii cultivars, the Pugster series is bred to be sterile or very low-seeding, largely eliminating the self-seeding invasiveness concern associated with standard butterfly bush in parts of the country, so it can be planted more responsibly near natural areas. It blooms from early summer through frost with only light deadheading needed to keep flowers coming, and like all butterfly bush it is a strong draw for butterflies, particularly swallowtails and monarchs, as well as hummingbirds. In zone 9, plants die back partially in winter and resprout vigorously from the base in spring; cut back hard in late winter to encourage a full flush of new flowering growth. Its small stature makes it a good fit for foundation plantings, mixed perennial borders, or large containers where a full-sized butterfly bush would overwhelm the space.
